sections.heading: Executive Overview
sections.body: This roadmap defines the transition from a fragmented, data-center–centric environment to a secure, cloud-first target architecture aligned to the enterprise growth strategy through FY2029. Current IT spend is weighted 72% toward maintaining 214 legacy applications, limiting investment in digital channels, analytics, and automation. The proposed program reallocates 28% of run-cost savings into business-critical capabilities, including customer lifecycle management, real-time supply chain visibility, and advanced risk analytics. The transformation is structured in phased increments to minimize operational disruption while accelerating value realization.

sections.heading: Target State Architecture
sections.body: 4HANA instance, replacing three regional ERPs and 46 satellite finance tools. Identity and access management will be centralized under a zero-trust security model with conditional access policies and continuous monitoring via a unified SIEM platform. Enterprise data will be governed through a cloud-native data lakehouse architecture, enabling standardized reporting and AI-driven insights.

sections.heading: Legacy System Decommissioning Plan
sections.body: A structured retirement plan targets 87 high-cost or redundant systems for decommissioning by Q4 2028, beginning with the Orion billing platform and the Atlas inventory management suite. Each application is categorized by business criticality, technical debt score, and integration complexity to determine migration sequencing. Data archival and regulatory retention requirements are addressed through immutable storage and automated metadata tagging prior to shutdown. Estimated annual savings from infrastructure, licensing, and support contracts are projected at $18.4M once the first two waves are completed.

sections.heading: Investment Priorities and Funding Model
sections.body: Capital allocation for FY2026–FY2029 prioritizes digital revenue channels, cybersecurity modernization, and process automation within Finance and Operations. Approximately $64M is earmarked for cloud migration and application refactoring, offset by a planned 15% reduction in on-premise hosting costs by 2027. A value-tracking framework links each funded initiative to defined business capabilities, measurable KPIs, and cost-to-serve reductions. Governance oversight will be provided by the Architecture Review Board and the Enterprise Investment Committee to ensure strategic alignment.

sections.heading: Business Capability Alignment
sections.body: The roadmap directly supports the enterprise capability model, with emphasis on Customer Engagement, Intelligent Operations, and Regulatory Compliance. Capability heat-mapping conducted in November 2025 identified significant maturity gaps in digital onboarding, predictive maintenance, and enterprise data governance. Target architecture components have been prioritized based on their ability to close these gaps within 24–36 months. Quarterly reviews will assess progress against capability maturity benchmarks and adjust sequencing as business demand evolves.

structure.heading: Legacy Decommissioning and Investment Roadmap with Financial and Risk Outcomes
text_content: **Legacy Decommissioning and Investment Roadmap with Financial and Risk Outcomes**

We will decommission 18 legacy applications by 30 Jun 2028 under the sponsorship of the Chief Information Officer and the Enterprise Architecture Board. The program is phased: 1) discovery and risk assessment (Q3–Q4 2025), 2) staged migration and integration (2026–2027), and 3) cutover and shutdown (Q1–Q2 2028). A designated Program Manager will report monthly to the CIO and quarterly to the Finance and Audit committees, tracking technical dependencies, data migration completion, and contractual termination milestones. This timeline is Executive-approved and resourced.

The program will reduce annual run cost from $48M in 2025 to $33M in 2028, a reduction of $15M (31.25%). Finance will record these reductions as realizations against the IT operating baseline and report quarterly to the Chief Financial Officer. Savings will be reallocated to sustainment of target-state platforms and to fund capability uplift prioritized by Business Units. The run-cost target supports a sustainable OPEX profile for FY2029 planning and enables a clearer payback window for new platform investments initiatives.

Change investment of $60M will be allocated across 2026–2028 to deliver migration, integration, and modernization activities. The CIO, in partnership with Finance and Business Sponsors, will publish an annual budget breakdown and quarterly burn forecasts; baseline KPIs include schedule adherence, escape defects, and value realization. A 10% contingency reserve will be held centrally for unforeseen integration complexity and vendor transition costs. Risk-adjusted decision gates at the end of each fiscal year will re-prioritize remaining funds to maximize business capability outcomes.

structure.full_text:
Enterprise IT Strategy & Target Architecture Roadmap (FY2026–FY2029)
Ref: EA-STRAT-29B | Date: 04 September 2026 | Prepared by: Office of the Chief Enterprise Architect

Section Executive Overview
This roadmap defines the transition from a fragmented, data-center–centric technology landscape to a secure, cloud-first target architecture aligned to priority business capabilities. The current estate includes 214 applications across six legacy platforms, with 38% classified as redundant or underutilized. Our strategy consolidates these systems into a unified digital platform emphasizing modular services, enterprise data governance, and zero-trust security. The transformation is structured over three fiscal years to balance operational stability with accelerated modernization.

Section Target State Architecture
The target architecture centers on a hybrid cloud foundation leveraging Azure Government regions and containerized workloads orchestrated through Kubernetes. Core business capabilities—Customer Onboarding, Claims Processing, Supply Chain Visibility, and Regulatory Reporting—will be supported through domain-aligned microservices and API-first integration. A centralized data platform built on Snowflake and governed through an enterprise data catalog will replace siloed reporting databases. Identity and access management will be standardized under a single Azure AD tenant with multi-factor authentication and conditional access policies.

Section Legacy System Decommissioning Plan
Between Q1 FY2027 and Q4 FY2028, 62 legacy applications hosted on the Orion, DeltaMain, and Mercury ERP platforms will be retired. Decommissioning will occur in phased waves tied to capability migration milestones, with dual-run periods limited to 90 days to mitigate operational risk. Estimated annual run-cost savings total $8.4M, primarily from data center hosting, proprietary licensing, and specialized support contracts. Data archival and regulatory retention requirements will be addressed through immutable cloud storage prior to shutdown.

Section Investment Priorities and Funding Allocation
Total transformation investment is projected at $46.7M over three years, with 52% allocated to platform engineering and cloud migration activities. Cybersecurity enhancements, including endpoint detection and zero-trust network segmentation, account for 18% of funding. Business capability enablement—specifically automation within Claims Processing and digital self-service for Customer Onboarding—represents 21% of planned spend. Remaining funds are reserved for change management, workforce reskilling, and contingency risk mitigation.

Section Business Capability Alignment
The roadmap is anchored to the enterprise capability map approved by the Strategy Council in June 2026. Technology investments are prioritized based on measurable impact to revenue growth, regulatory compliance posture, and operational cycle time reduction. For example, modernization of the Supply Chain Visibility capability is expected to reduce order reconciliation time by 35% and improve inventory accuracy to 98.5%. Governance checkpoints at each release increment ensure architectural compliance and direct traceability from solution delivery to business outcomes.

Confidential — Internal Distribution Only | Page 1 of 4
